subject: Finova: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Performance targets & regional routing (Finova / Redwood)

Hi Liam / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goal: low-latency inference for customer-facing product recommendations across US/EU/APAC.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~400 QPS globally with regional bursts up to ~800 QPS; peak concurrency per model ~100-150.
- Latency SLOs (customer-expecting): p95 target by region (confirm below).
- Streaming: some endpoints will stream partial tokens for perceived latency (typing / live suggestions).
- Data residency: EU customer data (and logs for EU tenants) must stay in EU; APAC has similar constraints for several customers.

Action items / asks for your confirmation:
1) Confirm target p95 latency per region. From call I captured: US ~150ms, EU ~220ms, APAC ~300ms — please confirm.
2) Confirm typical request size: average prompt tokens and expected maximum sequence length (tokens in + tokens out).
3) Confirm whether logs/audit trails must be stored in-region versus can be forwarded to a central location (we can support both).
4) Any SSO/KMS or SOC2 evidence we should prepare ahead of a technical deep dive?

Attachments: redwood-performance-slo-sheet.xlsx (working doc with suggested configuration + tradeoffs).

Next suggested step: 30–45 minute technical sync with Aditya (infra) and Rishi (solutions) — are you available Thurs or Fri this week?

Thanks — looking forward to narrowing the SLOs so we can lay out an architecture for regional routing.
—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets & regional routing (Finova / Redwood)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Confirming the numbers from our side and adding a few specifics:

- Latency SLOs (p95, tail): US <= 150ms, EU <= 220ms, APAC <= 300ms. These are customer-facing targets we need to hit for the recommendation endpoint.
- Throughput: steady ~400 QPS global; regional distribution roughly 50% US / 30% EU / 20% APAC. Bursts up to ~800 QPS for flash events.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent requests per model ~80–120; we plan to scale horizontally for peaks.
- Streaming: yes, we need chunked streaming for the autocomplete endpoint — partial tokens should be flushed every ~50ms when available.
- Request sizes: avg prompt ~120 tokens in, expected avg response ~40 tokens out (so ~160 tokens total). Max length up to ~1024 in/out for certain workflows.
- Data residency: EU customer data and logs must remain in EU; for APAC customers, similarly prefer regional residency. We will provide the formal residency requirements doc (attached).

Attaching: finova-data-residency-reqs.pdf.

Next steps: technical sync Thursday 14:00 CEST / 05:00 PT works for Priya and me. If that slots with your team, we can lock it.
—
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
liam.oconnor@finova.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets & regional routing (Finova / Redwood)

Thanks Liam — this is very helpful and aligns with what we expected. A few notes from our side ahead of the tech sync: 

- Feasibility: the targets look achievable. For p95 <=150ms in US, we recommend either hosted+dedicated hybrid (hosted for non-sensitive workloads; dedicated GPU pools pinned in-region for EU/APAC customers with residency constraints) or full Dedicated in EU/APAC if you need strict isolation.
- Routing: we support policy-based smart routing (latency vs cost), with automatic fallback to compatible model variants in other regions if regional capacity is temporarily constrained. For strict residency requirements, we can lock routing to region-only and fall back to degraded modes (e.g., quantized model that stays in-region).
- Streaming: our runtime supports low-latency partial token flushes. We'll need to tune batching windows and per-connection flush thresholds to meet the ~50ms flush target — this may affect throughput/cost tradeoffs.
- Logging & audit: we can keep logs/audit trails in-region (separate storage buckets per region) and integrate with your KMS for encryption-at-rest.

I've attached a short SLA/architecture note (redwood-sla-overview.pdf) and updated the SLO sheet with the numbers you provided. Please take a look before the sync.

Proposed agenda for the tech sync (30–45m):
1) Confirm token sizes & traffic shape (Liam)
2) Regional deployment options (Dedicated vs hosted + dedicated EU/APAC pools) (Aditya)
3) Streaming latency tuning and batching tradeoffs (Rishi / infra)
4) Data residency / logs / KMS integration (Security)
5) Next steps / timeline / PoC scope
\Thursday 14:00 CEST works for us — Aditya, Rishi: can you join?
—
Marissa Cole

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets & regional routing (Finova / Redwood)

Thanks all — quick technical responses and constraints from infra side: 

- Regional latency: achievable with dedicated regional pools sized for your steady-state and burst. For US p95=150ms we'll size the pool with GPU types optimized for low-latency inference and use continuous batching at small windows. EU/APAC targets are achievable but will need slightly larger pools due to network tail variability.
- Concurrency & throughput: to support 400 QPS steady and 800 QPS burst with ~80–120 concurrency per model, we'll provision autoscaling policies with headroom. If you need hard guarantees we recommend reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) with a commit for the peak tiers.
- Streaming: meeting ~50ms partial flush requirement is possible but tradeoffs exist — smaller batching window increases egress and GPU scheduling churn. We should instrument token latencies during PoC and tune flush thresholds per route.
- Data residency: we can pin storage and serving to region. For EU-only residency we will deploy private storage buckets and dedicated control plane connectors; logs can be kept in-region for the retention you specify. We will need the formal residency doc (attached) and access requirements for KMS.

Open question: can you share expected percent of streaming vs non-streaming traffic (rough %) and expected avg tokens per request during peak? That will help us size the PoC and estimate cost tradeoffs.

I can join Thursday 14:00 CEST; sending a calendar invite now.
—
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
